svg.title: Thirty Days to an Evidence-Ready Operating Desk
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-thirty-day-launch-sprint; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Thirty Days to an Evidence-Ready Operating Desk; subtitle: Four weekly milestones establish capability, not booked annual revenue.; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Milestones are operating targets. Required licenses and access permissions may take longer than this sprint; affected activities remain paused. The canonical time to first deal is 2–5 months.; caption: Day 30 should produce a working acquisition and diagnostic system, signed scope where available, and clear next actions. Do not convert a diagnostic estimate into collected fee revenue.; stages: label: Days 1-7; value: Define authority, scope, and unit economics; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Choose one employer segment and initial service rail. Build a state-activity licensing matrix, draft engagement and disclosure documents, obtain coverage quotes, and reconcile the $535,000 Base revenue and $294,250 expense model.; label: Days 8-14; value: Build secure intake and renewal intelligence; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Configure access controls and secure transfer, test intake with synthetic records, and research 50 deduplicated employers from public filings. Confirm renewal dates directly and avoid placing health records in the CRM.; label: Days 15-21; value: Run discovery and one bounded diagnostic; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Target five completed discovery calls and one signed diagnostic scope. With required authority and access in place, reconcile a limited PBM or E-Mod sample; otherwise continue testing only with synthetic records.; label: Days 22-30; value: Deliver evidence and schedule the commercial path; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Present a reproducible findings pack separating potential employer savings from operator fees. Identify contract restrictions, risk owners, implementation dates, and collection conditions; schedule renewal follow-up inside the realistic 2–5 month first-deal window.

text.title: Thirty Days to an Evidence-Ready Operating Desk
text.tspan: Thirty Days to an Evidence-Ready Operating Desk

circle.title: label: Days 1-7; value: Define authority, scope, and unit economics; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Choose one employer segment and initial service rail. Build a state-activity licensing matrix, draft engagement and disclosure documents, obtain coverage quotes, and reconcile the $535,000 Base revenue and $294,250 expense model.

text.title: Define authority, scope, and unit economics

circle.title: label: Days 8-14; value: Build secure intake and renewal intelligence; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Configure access controls and secure transfer, test intake with synthetic records, and research 50 deduplicated employers from public filings. Confirm renewal dates directly and avoid placing health records in the CRM.

text.title: Build secure intake and renewal intelligence

circle.title: label: Days 15-21; value: Run discovery and one bounded diagnostic; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Target five completed discovery calls and one signed diagnostic scope. With required authority and access in place, reconcile a limited PBM or E-Mod sample; otherwise continue testing only with synthetic records.

text.title: Run discovery and one bounded diagnostic

circle.title: label: Days 22-30; value: Deliver evidence and schedule the commercial path; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Present a reproducible findings pack separating potential employer savings from operator fees. Identify contract restrictions, risk owners, implementation dates, and collection conditions; schedule renewal follow-up inside the realistic 2–5 month first-deal window.

text.title: Deliver evidence and schedule the commercial path

Assumptions: Milestones are operating targets. Required licenses and access permissions may take longer than this sprint; affected activities remain paused. The canonical time to first deal is 2–5 months.
